pages.text: Measure a quarter-litre of drinking water into a heat-safe vessel. A clay pot will serve; a copper kettle carries more, but pour away or transfer the excess before beginning. Waxed carriers belong far from the fire.

Choose bone that itself sings with resonance. Set the preparation beside a strong, steady fire and allow thirty-five turns for steeping. The vessel stays with the work. To abandon it is to lose both water and bone, though the vessel may be recovered.

The finished draught is small. Drink it to uncover a word of the Deep Tongue, then consult thy lexicon or return to writing that once resisted thee. No scrap of paper gives the knack: the work can be attempted without these notes.
